title: Chalkboard XOR Game
summary: Given an array of integers nums, Alice and Bob take turns erasing exactly one number from the array, with Alice starting first.
statement: Given an array of integers nums, Alice and Bob take turns erasing exactly one number from the array, with Alice starting first. If erasing a number results in the bitwise XOR of the remaining numbers being zero, the player who erases that number loses. If the bitwise XOR of the numbers is zero at the start, the player whose turn it is wins. Return true if Alice wins the game, assuming both players play optimally.
constraints: Players alternately erase one number, with Alice first.
A mover loses if the remaining XOR becomes zero; a player starting a turn with XOR zero wins.
Return whether Alice wins under optimal play.
reference_solution:
def alice_wins_xor_game(nums):
    from functools import reduce
    from operator import xor
    return len(nums)%2==0 or reduce(xor,nums,0)==0
known_wrong_solutions:
def alice_wins_xor_game(nums):
    from functools import reduce
    from operator import xor
    return len(nums)%2==1 or reduce(xor,nums,0)==0
def alice_wins_xor_game(nums):
    from functools import reduce
    from operator import xor
    return len(nums)%2!=0 or reduce(xor,nums,0)!=0
hints: A zero starting XOR wins by rule.
With nonzero XOR, every even-length position is winning and every odd-length position is losing under optimal play.
Check zero XOR or even length.
The XOR symmetry ensures an even position has a safe deletion, while an odd nonzero position cannot avoid handing over that structure.
editorial: The XOR symmetry ensures an even position has a safe deletion, while an odd nonzero position cannot avoid handing over that structure.

tests.explanation: The nonzero XOR and odd length force Alice into a losing position.
The starting XOR is zero, so Alice wins immediately.
